correctness.rationale: Each strictly positive weighted permutation evolution algebra has a_i>0 and permutation pi on n coordinates; T(x)_{pi(i)}=a_i x_i^2/sum_j a_j x_j^2 on the closed nonnegative simplex. On each pi-cycle, the recurrence gamma_pi(i)*a_i=gamma_i^2 uniquely determines positive diagonal gauge gamma via the explicit (2^ell-1)-th root, so H(x)_i=gamma_i x_i/sum gamma_j x_j conjugates T to U(y)_{pi(i)}=y_i^2/sum_j y_j^2. Coordinatewise powers commute with pi, giving exact U^t(y)_{pi^t(i)}=y_i^(2^t)/sum_j y_j^(2^t). If I is the set of tied maximizers of y, all other coordinate ratios shrink at rho^(2^t), rho<1, so each orbit phase-shadows u_{pi^t I} superexponentially. Any periodic y becomes fixed by some pure normalized power under pi^L, forcing uniform positive entries on its support; thus all and only 2^n-1 nonempty support uniforms are periodic, with least periods equal to orbit lengths of pi acting on subsets. The exact counts #Fix(T^r)=2^{c(pi^r)}-1 and least-period orbit Möbius formula follow; the single n-cycle case reduces to nonempty binary necklaces. Perturbing any tied maximum to a unique maximum shows all support-size>1 periodic orbits are unstable; strict-max neighborhoods contract and show vertex cycles attract. Pointwise convergence of every trajectory iff pi is the identity, since a moved vertex creates periodic motion. Finite checker independently enumerates all 873 permutations through dimension six and sample gauges; infinite-dimensional assertion is proved algebraically, not inferred from finite tests.
